items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Oh, yeah, a little boy, George Washington.

ctx.x: Who were some of the good trombone players down here when you were young?

Morris French, Kid Ory, Jack Keran, and let's see who else I can... Who was with Buddy Petit? Morris French was with Rene. I'm trying to... Oh, yeah, a little boy, George Washington. He never did come back. Little bit of fella. Played nice trombone.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: Earl Humphrey had the band then, that George Washington was playing

ctx.x: Did you ever have any battles of music in the places like, say, the Bows Club or any of those?

Well, I won two Cups, one at the Espinade Hall down there, against Chris Kelly. What's that, the Italian Hall? The Italian Hall, yeah, that's what it was, the Italian Hall, and I won another at the St. Elizabeth, off a band called, well it was Earl Humphrey had the band then, that George Washington was playing, and it used to have two bands and everybody had a little dance at them times. Two bands, one this corner. Earl Humphrey had a band with George Washington?
Earl Humphrey had a band with who in it?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Oh, he was nice with a trombone player.

ctx.x: He was a trombone player and he was around Chicago. He was with King Oliver for a while. I didn't even need him. I didn't need him. What about George Washington? What kind of a trombone player was he?
Oh, he was nice with a trombone player. For what? What kind of music? Oh, just swing stuff with jazz music. I don't think he was no good on them boxes or anything like that. Yeah.
But he could, the band, flip some, or whatever. He was around Chicago. He was around Chicago. He was with King Oliver for a while. I didn't need him.
